scenes.title: Package Managers (apt, brew, pip)
scenes.narration: Package managers install, update, and remove software for you, handling all the tricky dependencies behind the scenes.

scenes.title: Which Manager for What
bullets: apt installs system software on Debian and Ubuntu Linux servers.
brew installs command-line tools and apps on macOS.
pip installs Python libraries into your Python environment.
scenes.narration: Each package manager owns a different layer of your system. On Ubuntu-style servers, apt manages operating-system packages like databases and utilities. On a Mac, brew fills the same role for developer tools. And pip is Python's own manager, pulling in the libraries your data code depends on.

scenes.title: System vs. Language Packages
scenes.narration: System managers like apt and brew install tools available to the whole machine and usually require administrator rights. Language managers like pip install libraries scoped to a specific runtime, such as pandas for Python. As a rule, use the system manager for programs and the language manager for the code your project imports.

scenes.title: Common Commands
scenes.code:
sudo apt update && sudo apt install postgresql
brew install git
pip install pandas
pip install -r requirements.txt
scenes.narration: With apt you first update the package index, then install, often prefixed by sudo for admin rights. Brew installs a tool in a single word with no update step needed. The pip command adds a Python library, and pointing it at a requirements file installs every dependency a project lists at once.

scenes.text: Record your Python dependencies in requirements.txt so anyone can rebuild the exact same environment.
scenes.narration: Pinning your dependencies in a requirements file makes your work reproducible. Anyone, including your future self, can recreate the identical setup with one command.
